operational-example.copy: Use Stepper to show progress through a short, ordered sequence with a known current step.

scenario.title: Vehicle onboarding
rationale: Flow defines the state semantics: active/current uses action-primary and complete uses success.
The ZIP reference informs marker shape, connector rhythm, label scale, depth, halo, and enter motion.
The color tension is resolved in favor of Flow semantics while preserving the ZIP-inspired dimensional treatment.

rows.label: ZIP influence
rows.value: Shape, connector rhythm, depth, halo, and motion only.

items.rule: Shows number, active/current action-primary treatment, or completed success check. ZIP informs depth and motion without replacing Flow state color.
Shows relationship and completed progress with success state color.
Names each step with compact text that can wrap by orientation.
Uses bounded enter motion for the active marker and completed check.

items: Mark the current step with aria-current step.
Do not make future steps clickable unless a pattern owns the rules.
Use Progress Indicator instead for non-step loading.

variants.copy: Stepper has two package-backed layout variants: horizontal and vertical. Density changes scale through Flow context. Compact, review, optional, blocked, error, routing, and recovery are not closed Stepper variants.

states.copy: Stepper state is derived from the current index: previous steps are complete with success color, the current step is active with Flow action-primary, and later steps are pending.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls orientation, state is derived from current progress, and density controls scale. Process errors, blockers, route guards, and future-step navigation belong to patterns.

full-width.copy: Stepper may fill a form header, but each marker, connector, and label must keep stable geometry.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use horizontal Stepper for roomy screens and vertical Stepper when labels need more space.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Stepper for short sequences. Use routes or templates for long processes and Tabs for parallel sections.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Prefer vertical when labels need room.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use horizontal for three to five steps.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use small density for dense setup systems.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify current step, orientation, density, and state derivation.

api-foundations.copy: Stepper API exposes steps, current index, orientation, and density while Design System foundations own sequence semantics, symbols, motion, and accessibility.

props.name: steps
props.notes: Ordered step labels and optional descriptions.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for parallel views.
Do not use for long navigation trees.
Do not make future steps clickable unless a pattern owns the rule.

groups.title: Review
items: Check aria-current, label wrap, connector state, complete success color, active action token, current gradient/depth, selected-step motion, mobile orientation, and completed checks.

mustTest: Active/current marker uses Flow action-primary and complete marker uses Flow success
rejectIf: Future steps are clickable without pattern rules.
Blocked, error, review, optional, or route behavior is presented as closed component behavior.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Stepper as sequence governance: agents can propose it for short ordered sequences, but humans confirm whether the system is truly sequential and whether routing or recovery should escalate to a pattern.
canDecide: Use for three to five ordered steps.
Use vertical orientation when labels need room.
Use completed checks for finished steps.
mustAsk: A blocked or error step needs recovery rules.
rejectIf: The system is parallel rather than sequential.
There are too many steps for a wizard.
The current step is not explicit.
Routing, validation, recovery, or future-step navigation is hidden inside the component.
miel.handoff: I am using Stepper for a short ordered sequence. Please confirm steps, current index, orientation, and whether routing or recovery should escalate to a pattern.
